building: Virginia C. Meredith Residence Hall South

criteria.name: Identity and provenance
evidence: Official Purdue BuildingShapes snapshot names FID 410 “Virginia C. Meredith Residence Hall South”, MRDS, address 1225 1st Street.
Purdue Newsroom opening article and the supplied photo identify Meredith South; its address and official BEP corroborate the intended building.
deductions: GIS snapshot edit date is unavailable and polygon accuracy is not survey-certified.

criteria.name: Plan geometry and placement
evidence: Fresh reopen check reports the structural shell’s source-derived XY bounds within 0.000022 m of transformed FID 410 bounds.
Asset preserves campus coordinates and stable asset/export collection.
deductions: Only axis-aligned bounds were independently checked in this review; they do not prove every edge, orientation or placement marker. Project conversion is a local approximation, not surveyed control.

criteria.name: Exterior silhouette and openings
evidence: Front preview now shows a taller west section and lower adjoining wings, matching Purdue BEP’s A=8 floors and B/C=6 floors.
Preview includes broad dark glazed vertical bays, a glazed base, a First Street canopy with columns, and two east retail sign panels, addressing the prior major gaps.
Official 2020 Purdue photo shows brick residential wings, glazed vertical study/stair bays, a ground-floor public base, and a projecting canopy.
deductions: Only one compass-untagged exterior photograph is available. Reverse-side features and the exact glazing-bay corner remain unverified.
The reverse preview still has a stack of large white triangular/wedge-like projections at the far west end. No inspected reference confirms these forms; they may be geometry artifacts.
The large glazed bays read as broad dark blue-green blocks at the overview scale; their frame divisions and exact proportions are not well resolved.
Purdue sources identify the east retail frontage, but the render overview does not make the two storefronts legible.

criteria.name: Materials and facade
evidence: The revised red-brown brick is substantially closer to the Purdue source image; dark window frames, glazed bays and pale canopy/trim are present.
deductions: Brick remains a uniform procedural field at overview scale; source image has visible masonry variation and stronger trim/frame separation. Glass reads nearly opaque in the renders.

criteria.name: Interior / cutaway
evidence: Fresh-opened asset contains corridor floors, room partitions, double beds and desks across levels 1–8; a level-3 plan view is supplied.
Purdue Residences gives a typical room illustration dimension of 11 ft 4 in × 16 ft 4 in; the modeler documents using it as a module estimate.
deductions: The level-3 view is an abstract linear diagram rather than a verified plan. The inspected sources do not establish the building-wide room layout or partition locations.
Shared bathrooms, lounges and other documented pod program are not clearly distinguished in the provided level-3 view.

criteria.name: Presentation and technical quality
evidence: Exact saved asset fresh-opened in Blender 5.2.3; expected `Asset_massing_meredith_hall_south_ffbc444` contains 56 objects (54 meshes).
Reopen check reports closed structural wall, roof and basement meshes with zero boundary/nonmanifold edges; no external image dependencies are reported.
Front/reverse exterior and level-3 plan review renders are available.
deductions: The unexplained west-end wedge projections remain visible in the reverse render and affect presentation quality.
The level-3 plan render is very low-contrast and hard to read as rooms, shared spaces and circulation.

evidence_sources.feature: FID 410, MRDS, Virginia C. Meredith Residence Hall South
evidence_sources.limitations: Map polygon; accuracy and feature edit date unavailable.

evidence_sources.use: Qualitative exterior material, glazing, entry and massing comparison; not dimensional evidence.

evidence_sources.provider: Purdue University Office of Emergency Preparedness
evidence_sources.use: Documents west A=8 floors, middle B=6 floors and basement, east C=6 floors; two retail food operations at first floor of east/C.
Ground-floor glass and east-end retail dining description; no dimensioned elevations inspected.
Typical single room illustration dimensions 11 ft 4 in × 16 ft 4 in; illustration is not a building-wide floor plan.
Large ground-floor glazing and residence program.

findings.location: far west end in reverse preview
findings.finding: Six large white triangular/wedge forms protrude from the facade, with no inspected source support.
findings.required_correction: Verify against a reverse-side photo or remove/refine if these are accidental geometry; document their source if intentional.

findings.finding: Two retail sign panels are represented, but storefront identities/frontage are not legible in the overview render.
findings.required_correction: Provide a closer review render and distinguish Panera and QDOBA entries/signs.

findings.finding: The schematic shows a long corridor and repeated room modules, but the supplied image does not make room boundaries, bathrooms or lounge pods easy to inspect.
findings.required_correction: Render a closer high-contrast plan and label or visually separate corridor, rooms, bathrooms and lounge zones. Keep unverified plan dimensions marked as estimates.

uncertainties: Only one official exterior facade photo is available and it is not compass-tagged; other facades and the exact entrance/glazing orientation remain unverified.
GIS bounds match closely, but this review did not independently recompute every polygon edge or the master placement.
Story count is supported by Purdue BEP, but floor-to-floor and total heights are model estimates.
Room modules use Purdue Residences typical-room illustration dimensions; actual building-wide layout and bathroom/lounge placement remain unverified.
No master integration review was performed.
